@graph.name: hydrogenation_rdy_2026_09

Preparation
@graph.schema:description: Everything done before the main operation starts: charging, setting up, closing the apparatus.

@graph.schema:name: Work-up
@graph.schema:description: Everything done after the main operation: sampling, emptying, separating, washing, concentrating, purifying, analysing.

@graph.schema:name: Transcribing the masses into the spreadsheet
@graph.schema:description: The masses of RDY, the product and the dimer over the run - the weighed RDY charge and the masses from 'Analysing the final reaction mixture by GC' - were typed by hand into one spreadsheet per experiment.

@graph.schema:name: Analysing the final reaction mixture by GC
@graph.schema:description: Gas chromatography of the final reaction mixture. One injection, one chromatogram: the adiponitrile left over, the hexamethylenediamine formed and the dimeric by-product are read off it as three separate peaks, which is why this is one measurement with three results rather than three measurements.

@graph.schema:name: Assuming no product is present at the start
@graph.schema:description: Nothing containing hexamethylenediamine was charged, so its mass at the start is taken as zero rather than measured.

@graph.schema:name: Assuming no dimer is present at the start
@graph.schema:description: Nothing containing the dimer was charged, so its mass at the start is taken as zero rather than measured.

@graph.schema:name: Weighing in the RDY charge
@graph.schema:description: The adiponitrile charge is weighed on the bench balance before it is added to the vessel.

@graph.schema:name: Logging the pressure
@graph.schema:description: The transmitter on the vessel records the pressure over the whole run; the values are the time series in the data file.

@graph.schema:name: Controlling the pressure
@graph.schema:description: The regulator in the hydrogen line holds the vessel at the set pressure by feeding gas on demand.

@graph.schema:name: Setting the stirring speed
@graph.schema:description: The speed course of the stirrer (up to 1200 rpm, hold, back to 0) is set on the stirrer before it runs.

@graph.schema:name: Logging the temperature
@graph.schema:description: The probe in the vessel records the temperature of its contents over the whole run; the values are the time series in the data file.

@graph.schema:name: Controlling the temperature
@graph.schema:description: The jacket holds the contents at the set temperature of the run.

@graph.schema:name: Metering the hydrogen uptake
@graph.schema:description: The mass flow meter totalises the hydrogen fed to the sparger; its running total is the recorded 'H2 used'.

@graph.schema:name: Assuming the sample volume
@graph.schema:description: The volume drawn with the syringe and pushed into the GC vial is taken as 1 mL: the syringe holds 1 mL, and a GC vial holds 1.5-2 mL and is usually filled with about 1 mL. The volume actually drawn was not recorded.

@graph.schema:name: Adding the solid RDY
@graph.schema:description: The weighed adiponitrile is charged into the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Adding the catalyst
@graph.schema:description: The platinum catalyst is charged into the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Adding the liquid
@graph.schema:description: Water and isopropanol are charged into the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Sparging
@graph.schema:description: Hydrogen is fed through the sparger into the liquid for the whole run.

@graph.schema:name: Stirring
@graph.schema:description: The stirrer runs at the set speed for the whole run, dispersing the gas in the liquid.

@graph.schema:name: Cooling
@graph.schema:description: Coolant flows through the jacket to carry off the heat of reaction.

@graph.schema:name: Removing the liquid
@graph.schema:description: The reaction mixture is discharged from the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Removing the catalyst
@graph.schema:description: The catalyst is recovered from the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Removing the solid RDY
@graph.schema:description: Adiponitrile left unconverted is taken out of the vessel through its opening.

@graph.schema:name: Running the hydrogenation
@graph.schema:description: The run itself: hydrogen on, stirrer on, cooling on, everything recorded.

@graph.schema:name: Drawing the sample
@graph.schema:description: A syringe takes about 1 mL of the reaction mixture out of the vessel after the run and transfers it into a GC vial. Drawn before the vessel is emptied - afterwards the liquid is already outside the system and cannot be sampled any more.

@graph.schema:name: Putting on the lid
@graph.schema:description: The glass lid is put on the vessel once everything is charged; from here on the vessel is closed.

@graph.schema:name: Taking off the lid
@graph.schema:description: The lid is taken off before the vessel is emptied by pouring out.

@graph.schema:description: Charging and emptying happen by hand and the coolant and the sparged gas are visible while they flow, so every one of these port crossings was seen to happen. @graph.schema:description: Not observed, a modelling choice for this example: while the vessel is open for charging (see 'Assuming when the vessel and the vial were open'), nitrogen and oxygen of the room air are assumed to enter the headspace.
